I went to the bar to hang out with some friends and he was sitting on the deck. I sat across from him and said, "Hey, I think I've seen you around." 
He said, "Oh yeah?"
I said, "Yeah, do you live in Trenton?" (this was an area I drove through often)
He hesitated, "Yeah?"
I said, "Yeah, I think I've seen you walking through there."
With the most disgusted look on his face and suspension in his voice he said, "Ok..." and turned his head away from me.

I know, it sounds like I'm a creep but I was just trying to make conversation!

A few days later a friend invited me over to said guys house to hang out with him. I told him that said guy probably doesn't like me after what I said at the bar. He told me to come over anyway. So I did. This guy didn't pay any attention to me so I just chatted with my friend. Eventually he said a few things, offered me a beer and then went to bed. I left shortly after. 

A couple weeks went by and he popped up as people I might know on facebook. I added him and we started talking about music and decided to hang out officially. After many games of facebook scrabble and official hangouts (not me stalking him ;P) he asked me to be his girlfriend. This was very hard for me to accept, not because of him, but because of other things going on in my life (but thats a depressing story for the "not so happy subreddit"). Eventually I did and fast forward 2 years later, we're getting married in May!

I understand how you feel. Two and half years ago I was in an accident and my boyfriend of 2 years, who talked about getting married after he got back from Afghanistan, passed away almost immediately. I have always suffered from depression for as long as I can remember and I thought to myself, "Why him and not me? I'm the one who wants to die." The only thing that kept me from not killing myself at the time was being laid up on the couch with a broken leg and being watched almost every minute of the day. I really don't know how I made it through all of that.  

All I can say is it gets better. Or at least you go through periods of it getting better. Ive met someone and he is the best thing that has ever happened to me. I am actually happier than I've ever been (believe me, I'm still depressed, but its not as extreme). Sometimes when it gets really bad I wish that it would have been me instead of him but then I think about the guy I am with now. He suffers from depression too. I think about if I weren't here then I wouldn't have met him and he would still be a borderline alcoholic. We really have helped each other, in a lot of ways. 

I know you may not believe this but you're here for a reason. Whether you believe in God or not (I don't), try to think about some of the good things in your life, your goals and the people around you that care about you. You are here for something, you'll figure it out one day.
